query: SELECT type, name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table','view') ORDER BY name
result: Eight tables: attendance, budget, event, expense, income, major, member, zip_code. No views. Declared foreign keys: attendance(link_to_event->event.event_id, link_to_member->member.member_id), budget(link_to_event->event.event_id), expense(link_to_budget->budget.budget_id, link_to_member->member.member_id), income(link_to_member->member.member_id), member(link_to_major->major.major_id, zip->zip_code.zip_code).
validation_method: read-only schema inspection of the SQLite file

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM each of attendance, budget, event, expense, income, major, member, zip_code
result: attendance 326, budget 52, event 42, expense 32, income 36, major 113, member 33, zip_code 41877.

query: SELECT position, COUNT(*) FROM member GROUP BY position ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
result: Member 26, Inactive 3, Vice President 1, Treasurer 1, Secretary 1, President 1. Six distinct values; Member and Inactive are participation states while the remaining four are office titles.

query: SELECT type, status, COUNT(*) FROM event GROUP BY type, status
result: Types: Meeting 16, Guest Speaker 7, Game 6, Social 4, Community Service 4, Election 2, Budget 2, Registration 1. Statuses: Closed 18, Open 13, Planning 11. Every type except Registration appears with more than one status.

query: SELECT status, SUM(event_date < '2020-01-01'), COUNT(*) FROM event GROUP BY status
result: Closed: 18 of 18 events dated before 2020. Open: 2 of 13 before 2020. Planning: 0 of 11 before 2020. All Closed events are 2019 events and all Planning events are 2020 events.

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT link_to_event, link_to_member FROM attendance GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)
result: 0 duplicate pairs, confirming the pair of event and member identifies an attendance record. 30 distinct members and 17 distinct events appear; attendance per event ranges from 4 to 30 with mean 19.18.
validation_method: primary key uniqueness check and grouped counts

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id) and the member analogue
result: 25 of 42 events have no attendance record, and 3 of 33 members never appear in attendance. Attendance therefore covers 17 events and 30 members.

query: SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(*) FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event HAVING COUNT(*) > 1; SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event)
result: 15 events hold more than one budget line, with a maximum of 4 lines on a single event. 52 budget lines map to 23 distinct events.

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM budget WHERE ABS(COALESCE(spent,0)+COALESCE(remaining,0)-COALESCE(amount,0)) > 0.01
result: 0 mismatches out of 52 rows: spent + remaining equals amount on every budget line. No nulls in spent, remaining or amount. Amounts range 10 to 350 (total 4200); one remaining value is negative (-0.199999999999999).
validation_method: arithmetic identity check across all rows

query: SELECT b.budget_id, b.category, b.spent, (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(x.cost),0) FROM expense x WHERE x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id) FROM budget b
result: The spent amount of each budget line equals the sum of the costs of the expenses charged to that line, verified across all 52 lines. Budget lines with no expenses carry a spent amount of 0.

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.event_status <> e.status
result: 0 disagreements: the status recorded on each budget line matches the status of its event on every joined row. budget.event_status holds the same three values as event.status.

query: SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM budget GROUP BY category ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
result: Food 22, Advertisement 15, Speaker Gifts 7, Parking 7, Club T-Shirts 1. Five distinct categories across 52 lines.

query: SELECT approved, COUNT(*) FROM expense GROUP BY approved
result: The only non-null value is the text true, on 31 rows; 1 row is null. No false value and no numeric encoding are present.

query: SELECT MIN(cost), MAX(cost), ROUND(SUM(cost),2) FROM expense
result: Costs range from 6.0 to 295.12 with a total of 2086.05 across 32 expenses, stored as real values with fractional precision.

query: SELECT source, COUNT(*) FROM income GROUP BY source ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
result: Dues 33, Sponsorship 1, School Appropration 1, Fundraising 1. Four distinct values; the appropriation label is stored with the literal spelling School Appropration.

query: SELECT income_id, link_to_member, source FROM income i WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member m WHERE m.member_id = i.link_to_member)
result: 3 receipts have a null member link: recN3WFwGR0c17xe2 (Fundraising), recenMwUQktMpDTQc (School Appropration), recphAFPbyclQY63d (Sponsorship). All three are non-dues sources; every dues receipt carries a member link.

query: SELECT MIN(amount), MAX(amount), SUM(amount) FROM income
result: Amounts are whole numbers from 50 to 3000 with a total of 5850 across 36 receipts. The column affinity is integer, unlike the fractional expense and spent columns.
validation_method: aggregate range, total and value type check

query: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM income; SELECT ROUND(SUM(cost),2) FROM expense; SELECT SUM(amount) FROM budget; date ranges per table
result: Total income 5850 against total expense 2086.05, giving a net balance of 3763.95; total budgeted allocation 4200. Receipt dates run 2019-09-01 to 2019-10-31 and expense dates 2019-08-20 to 2019-11-19, while event dates run 2019-09-01 to 2020-05-05.
validation_method: aggregate totals and per-table date range extraction

query: SELECT event_date FROM event ORDER BY event_date LIMIT 3 / DESC; the analogous queries on expense.expense_date and income.date_received
result: event.event_date values are ISO-8601 date-times with a T separator, e.g. 2019-09-01T07:00:00 and 2020-05-05T12:00:00. expense.expense_date and income.date_received are date-only strings, e.g. 2019-08-20 and 2019-10-31.
validation_method: representative value sampling per date column

query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) FROM zip_code; SELECT type, COUNT(*) FROM zip_code GROUP BY type
result: 41877 postal codes covering 18729 distinct cities. Type values: Standard 29973, PO Box 9438, Unique 2466. City names repeat across postal codes, for example Abbeville holds 6 codes and Abilene 11.

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM member m LEFT JOIN zip_code z ON m.zip = z.zip_code WHERE z.zip_code IS NULL; and the state distribution
result: 0 orphan references and no null member zips: every member resolves to exactly one postal record. Members span 18 states, led by NY 5, NJ 4, MD 3, IN 3, IL 3.
validation_method: left-join integrity check and grouped distribution

query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT department), COUNT(DISTINCT college) FROM major; member LEFT JOIN major on link_to_major
result: 113 majors across 47 departments and 8 colleges. 32 of 33 members resolve to a major with 0 orphan references; 1 member has a null major link. College counts among members: College of Education & Human Services 8, College of Humanities and Social Sciences 7, College of Engineering 6, College of Agriculture and Applied Sciences 6, College of Natural Resources 2, School of Business 1.
validation_method: left-join integrity check and grouped distribution

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.budget_id IS NULL
result: 19 of 42 events have no budget row; 23 distinct events are covered by the 52 budget lines. No budget line has a null event link.

query: Left-join orphan checks from attendance, budget, expense and income to their referenced tables
result: attendance->event 0 orphans, attendance->member 0 orphans, budget->event 0 orphans, expense->budget 0 orphans, expense->member 0 orphans. expense.link_to_member and expense.link_to_budget are never null. income->member has 3 rows with a null link, which are excluded from this orphan count by the null test.
